title: Airport clip GX010474 still sideways in the Source monitor, still wide on its poster
wanted: See my first clip the right way up before I start
did: Made the new film from the folder; GX010474 opened in Source automatically; switched the Project panel to icon view
happened: Source shows a narrow tall picture with my friend's face lying on its side (90° turned), black bars both sides. Its poster in icon view is a normal wide picture of the same ceiling lights. The only hint is a tiny ↻ next to the name in list view whose hover text says 'Turned 90° the other way by the file's rotation flag; there is no sensor reading for this clip, so the flag is trusted.' I don't know what a rotation flag or sensor reading is, and nothing lets me turn it back. Same as COLD-08 last time.
expected: Poster and Source agree, and the clip is upright (the wide poster is the right way up); or a plain 'Rotate' control on the clip
where: Source monitor / Project panel, before first pass
suggestion: Trust the picture (faces, horizon) over the flag, or give a right-click Rotate 90°; say in plain words 'this clip was recorded with the camera turned'

title: Sideways clips quietly turn upright a minute into the pass, and the clip name is replaced by 'GX…  flag ignored'
wanted: Know which clips are sideways and whether the tool has dealt with them
did: Looked at GX010474/484/492 before the pass (sideways in Source), started the pass, came back to the Project list
happened: About a minute into the pass, without any message, the three clips' rows changed: the name shrank to 'GX…' and a grey chip 'flag ignored' appeared. GX010492 now plays upright and wide in Source (good). The chip's hover says 'Rotation flag ignored: the file says turn it 90° the other way, but the camera's sensor says it was shot upright.' So the fix exists, but only after the pass reads the sensors, and it speaks engineer ('flag', 'sensor'). I can no longer read which clip is which in the list: three rows are just 'GX…'. GX010474 then sat on 'preparing preview…' with a film-icon placeholder for over a minute.
expected: Upright from the start, or one line 'turned 3 clips upright (they were recorded with the camera on its side)'; the clip name stays readable
where: Project panel list view, Source monitor, during first pass
suggestion: Keep the full name, put the mark after it; word the chip 'turned upright'; do the sensor check at import, before anyone looks

title: GX010474 is labelled 'shot upright, flag ignored' but the Source monitor still plays it sideways
wanted: Trust the chip that says the airport clip has been put right
did: After the chip appeared I re-opened GX010474 in Source, waited out 'preparing preview…' (over a minute), clicked into the middle of the clip
happened: The Index says 'Rotation flag ignored: the file says turn it 90° the other way, but the camera's sensor says it was shot upright' with a dropdown 'let the sensor decide', yet the Source monitor shows a tall narrow picture with the bar and my friends lying on their side. GX010492, with the same chip, does show upright. So for this clip the words and the picture disagree, and I can't tell which the film will get.
expected: When the screen says upright, the picture is upright (or it says 'still preparing the upright preview')
where: Source monitor vs Index panel rotation line, during first pass
suggestion: Rebuild the Source preview when the orientation decision changes, and drop the old one at once

title: Progress panel contradicts itself: 'heard 26/26' above 'Listens to every clip… (7 of 26 clips still to do)'
wanted: Know how far the pass has got
did: Opened the running first pass panel at ~3 min
happened: Status line: 'heard 26/26 · looked at 19/26 · previews 4/26'. First bullet, about listening: '7 of 26 clips still to do'. The 7 seems to belong to looking, not listening. 'Takes about 3 minutes' also doesn't say whether that is what is left or the whole thing (it said 6 at the start).
suggestion: Tick bullets off as done; say 'about 3 minutes left'

title: The proposal opens on the sideways airport clip, and it plays sideways in the Program monitor
wanted: An opening shot the right way up
did: Ran the first pass (asked 90 s), pressed Play it, then clicked the ruler at 0:03 with playback stopped
happened: Shot 01 is GX010474 (22:16–30:01), the first 8 s of the film. The Program monitor shows it tall and narrow with black bars, the bar counter running vertically and my friends lying on their side. The AI's own clip description says 'a hand-held phone shot recorded sideways' and the Project row says 'flag ignored … the camera's sensor says it was shot upright' — three different stories, and the picture is the wrong one. Same as old COLD-13. A red 'unsupported' tag sits on this same shot.
expected: The opening shot upright, or the AI skips a clip it knows is sideways, or it tells me 'shot 1 is sideways: turn it?'
suggestion: Make the rotation decision once and have the Source, Program, the poster and the AI's description use it

title: After accepting, the Assistant asks 'What is this film about?' — I already told it before the pass
wanted: Get on with watching my cut
did: Typed a description in the first-pass box, accepted the proposal
happened: The Assistant tab opens with an empty box 'What is this film about? optional — a sentence is enough'. My sentence from the first pass box isn't there, so I wonder whether it was used at all.
suggestion: Show the sentence I gave, editable

title: Turning the sideways opening shot upright by hand takes two guesses and scale arithmetic
wanted: Turn shot 1 the right way up
did: Selected shot 1, Effect Controls › Motion › Rotation: typed 90 (upside down), then -90 (upright but a small box with black all round), then Scale 178
happened: It works in the end and the picture fills the frame upright, which proves the clip was a normal wide shot all along and the tool turned it. But I had to guess the direction and work out 178% myself; there is no 'Rotate 90°' on right-click, and the poster in Effect Controls and the timeline thumbnail stay sideways.
expected: A right-click 'Rotate 90° ⟲ / ⟳' on the clip that also fills the frame, or the clip's own 'Rotation' choice exposed in the Project panel (it exists only deep in the Index)
where: Effect Controls › Motion on timeline shot 1
suggestion: Put the Index's 'use the file's flag / ignore the flag' choice on the clip's right-click menu in plain words: 'Turn upright'

title: The AI's opening title comes out sideways on the shot I had turned upright
wanted: 'Copper Mountain · Feb 2026' across the opening shot
did: Selected shot 1 (which I had rotated -90° / scale 178 by hand), asked in the prompt box for an opening title, Accept, waited ~25 s
happened: The Program monitor at 0:02 shows the title running vertically up the right side of the picture, on a dark band, reading bottom-to-top. The AI's own plan text said 'The shot is rotated -90 and scaled 178, so place the title in the visible frame of the sequence', so it knew — and still turned the words with the picture. The card says ACCEPTED and 'reads “Copper Mountain · Feb 2026”' as if all is fine; nothing says it was checked against the frame.
expected: Titles sit on the film's frame, not inside the clip's rotation
where: Designed Effects title on a rotated shot, Program monitor
suggestion: Draw titles after the clip's Motion; and let the check look at the Program frame, which would have caught this

title: Asked to fix the sideways title; the AI says it is now 'level… left to right across the top', and it is still sideways
wanted: Get the title to read across the screen
did: Typed in the prompt box (scope Shot 1): 'The title you just made is sideways on screen. Make it read horizontally…'; Accept; waited ~35 s
happened: Good: it remembered which title I meant, said honestly 'I have not looked at these frames', guessed the cause (the shot's -90 rotation), and the new title replaced the old (old card shows REMOVED / Restore). Bad: the new card says 'redrawn level in the finished frame, reading left to right across the top of shot 1' and the Program monitor at 0:02 shows it still running vertically, now up the left edge. Two tries, two sideways titles, and the card's words describe a picture that isn't there.
expected: Either it's level, or the card says it could not check / looks wrong
where: Designed Effects card vs Program monitor, shot 1
suggestion: Check the title on the finished Program frame before writing 'level'

title: The clip's own Rotation choice in the Index changes nothing I can see
wanted: Turn GX010474 upright at the clip, so the Source, the timeline and the AI title all agree
did: Index tab › GX010474 › Rotation dropdown: switched 'let the sensor decide' to 'use the file's flag', waited 10 s, clicked into Source; then to 'ignore the flag', waited 10 s, clicked again
happened: The words beside it changed ('…you set this by hand') and the chip came and went, but the Source monitor showed the exact same sideways picture all three times. It's also the only clip-level rotate in the tool, buried in the Index's detail pane, which a newcomer would never find.
expected: Picking a rotation re-draws the clip that way everywhere
suggestion: Make it act at once and move it to the clip's right-click menu

title: '1 failed' after a title that worked, with no word on what failed
wanted: Know whether my title change went through
did: Asked for the title on shot 2 instead; Accept all (2 edits); waited ~2.5 min
happened: The title on shot 2 is level and readable — good. But the banner says '1 effect designed, 1 failed — review it in Designed Effects'. The failed one was presumably 'take it off shot 1', which I had already removed by hand, so nothing is wrong, but the word 'failed' made me go hunting. The whole round trip took about 2.5 minutes for one line of text, with nothing telling me how long.
where: Timeline banner after an AI title edit
suggestion: Say 'already gone from shot 1' instead of failed; show expected time for a title

title: Exported film opens sideways and zoomed in, although the Program monitor showed it upright
wanted: The file I send my friends to look like what I watched
did: Turned shot 1 upright by hand (Rotation -90°, Scale 178), checked it in the Program monitor, exported Quick 1080p, skimmed the file
happened: In the file, the first 7 s (GX010474, the airport bar) are sideways: the bar counter runs diagonally/vertically and my friends' faces lie on their side, and the picture is blown up so heads are cut off. The Program monitor showed it upright and whole right before export. Every other shot matches the Program monitor and the shot-2 title is there. So the very first thing my friends see is wrong, and nothing in the tool would have told me — I only know because I opened the file.
expected: Export = what the Program monitor shows
where: Export vs Program monitor, shot 1 (rotated clip)
suggestion: Apply clip rotation (flag/sensor + Motion) the same way in the monitor and the encoder; a one-frame compare of monitor vs export after rendering would catch it

title: After a page reload the airport clip is finally upright in Source, and my hand fix now turns it sideways in the Program monitor
wanted: Understand why the export was sideways
did: Reloaded the page (F5), clicked shot 1, double-clicked it to open in Source
happened: Source now shows GX010474 upright and wide for the first time this session. The Program monitor now shows shot 1 sideways and zoomed — exactly like the export — because my Rotation -90 / Scale 178 is now applied on top of an already-upright clip. So the Index rotation choice (COLD-10) or the sensor fix did take effect, but the Source and Program monitors kept drawing the old picture until a reload, and I made my 'fix' against a stale picture. The monitors lied for ~20 minutes, and the export told the truth.
expected: When a clip's rotation is decided or changed, both monitors redraw it at once
where: Source/Program after reload; follows COLD-10 and COLD-12
suggestion: Invalidate the cached preview/proxy and redraw immediately on any rotation change; show 'redrawing upright…'

title: Find says there's no one drinking from the milk jug (it's in my film), and labels its guess 'looks like “a dog”' from my previous search
wanted: Find the moment the milkman drinks from the jug
did: Selects › 'find a moment…': typed 'a dog', Enter (8 s, nothing); then 'someone drinking from the milk jug', Enter, waited ~20 s
happened: Answer: 'Nothing convincing like “someone drinking from the milk jug” in this footage. These are only the closest guesses.' The one guess is a black thumbnail captioned 'looks like “a dog”' — GX010499 at 0:14, 'seen by the 3080'. The jug drinking is in GX010495 (the AI used it as shot 13 itself: 'he raises the jug and drinks once more'). So Find missed a moment its own cut describes, and the caption is left over from the dog search. 'seen by the 3080' is jargon again.
expected: The GX010495 jug moment as the top hit; captions that match this search
suggestion: Search the clip descriptions and the AI's own shot notes first; clear old captions when a new search starts
